LESSON: THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT IN KENYA • THE EXECUTIVE, • THE LEGISLATURE • THE JUDICIARY

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Systems
Topic 4.4: The National Government in Kenya • The Executive, • The Legislature • The Judiciary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers The National Government in Kenya • The Executive, • The Legislature • The Judiciary, part of Political Systems in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How is work shared among the three arms of the Government in our country?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The National Government in Kenya • The Executive, • The Legislature • The Judiciary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: engage effectively with others as learners find out in groups the composition of the three arms of government in Kenya

using relevant sources.

• Creativity and Imagination: undertake tasks that help as learners illustrate and display in class the composition of the three arms of

National Government in Kenya.

Values:
• Responsibility: engages in assigned roles and duties as learners find out in groups, the composition of the three arms of government

in Kenya using relevant sources.

• Unity: appreciate effort of others as learners discuss, in groups functions of the three arms of National Government in Kenya.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Patriotism and good governance: good governance at all levels as learners Illustrate and display in class the composition of the

three arms of National Government in Kenya.

• Peace Education: learners appreciate similarities and differences amongst themselves as they brain storm in groups the three arms

of National Government in Kenya and share in class. (The Executive, the Legislature and the Judiciary).

Links to other Learning Areas:
English and Kenya Sign Language: learners apply the skills of effective communication and signing as they discuss the functions of the

three arms of National Government in Kenya.
